text:
harper: first-day snag  accepted the org invite but every push is denied (403). weirdly the audit email shows the invite was accepted by `harper-bot`? also the CI checks failed saying 'unknown committer'. who handles this? cc @mina

mina: hi harper, welcome! that audit oddness usually means the HR invite used the wrong github username mapping. can you paste the push error and `git config user.name` + `git config user.email`?

harper: push error:
```
$ git push origin feature/telemetry
remote: Permission to redwood-inference/service-api.git denied to harper-bot.
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-api.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403
```

and `git config user.email` -> harper@personal.example.com. I accepted the invite from my work account `harper.dev` though.

it-support: couple things to check: 1) are you pushing over HTTPS with a cached credential/token for `harper-bot`? 2) is your local commit author/email different from the account they provisioned for CI (makes CI flag unknown committer)? run `gh auth status` and `git remote -v` and paste outputs.

harper: `git remote -v` is `origin https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-api.git (fetch)` and `gh auth status` shows authenticated as `harper-bot` (what the heck). I never created that account.

mina: HR sometimes provisions GitHub accounts for contractors and reserves usernames like `harper-bot`. seems HR sent invite to that username and it got auto-claimed by the provisioning system when you accepted with an email alias. We'll need to re-send to `harper.dev`. For the immediate push problem, clear Git credential manager cache and re-login as your work user.

it-support: run:
```
# mac/linux
printf "url=https://github.com\n" | git credential-osxkeychain erase
# or
gh auth logout --hostname github.com && gh auth login
```
Also check macOS Keychain for any token entries named github.com and remove stale ones.

harper: removed keychain entries, logged out and `gh auth login` as `harper.dev`. But pushes still show remote denying permission; audit still shows `harper-bot` as the actor.

it-support: sounds like the invite accepted step created `harper-bot` as a GitHub account linked to your email. I will re-send the invite to `harper.dev` and update membership. If CI recorded your old email on commits, we can ask the CI team to whitelist the new committer identity or re-run checks once your pushes show the correct user.

it-support: re-sent invite to `harper.dev` and revoked `harper-bot` session for security. Also cleared pending SSO enforcement for the incorrect account. @ci-bot FYI: please re-run checks when user pushes with correct identity.

ci-bot: CI re-run queued for branch feature/telemetry after membership change.

harper: accepted new invite, re-logged in, and pushed — still failing initially until I did a `git config user.email harper@redwood.com` and amended the commit author on the top commit: `git commit --amend --reset-author` then force-pushed. That fixed the CI unknown committer issue.

mina: perfect. Follow-ups: 1) onboarding doc should warn about org invites being linked to pre-provisioned usernames (HR provisioning), 2) note to check local git commit email and `gh auth` separately, 3) add a short HR <> IT checklist so invites go to the right GH handle. I'll file a doc update.

onboarding-bot: Tip: if you see `harper-bot` or similar in audit logs, contact people-ops to correct the invite mapping before accepting invites.

harper: thanks everyone 389 happy to be in. Can someone add me to `service-team`?

it-support: added to service-team and eng-sdks. You should see repo access shortly. Closing thread 44d :white_check_mark:
